newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA Q2 matches analysts' estimates.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA Q2 matches analysts' estimates.

text.p: CompUSA Inc's second quarter earnings matched Wall Street's lowered expectations of $0.25 a share, according to First Call.
Analysts cut their estimates after CompUSA, one of the largest computer retailers, said in early January that Christmas sales were weak.

Comparable store sales rose 1.5 percent in the second quarter for the 95 stores open one year or more, in line with what CompUSA predicted in early January. Before it announced the weak holiday season sales, analysts had been forecasting a rise of about three percent.

CompUSA said earnings per share for the second quarter of fiscal 1997 ended December 28, 1996 were $0.25 compared with $0.20 last year. Sales grew 22 percent to $1.2 billion from $983 million for the second quarter of fiscal 1996.
James Halpin, CompUSA president and chief executive, said he was "pleased" with the results.

"CompUSA achieved record earnings despite the highly promotional environment during the holidays and slowdown in retail sales toward the end of the season. We believe these results demonstrate the strength of CompUSA's unique operating model and the dedication of our team members."
